newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends stable despite reform news.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends stable despite reform news.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar ended a trace higher on Friday, all but ignoring a central bank plan to ease restrictions on the types of income that can be used for foreign exchange forward trading from December 16.
The local dollar ended at T$27.494 to the U.S. dollar compared to Thursday's T$27.498 close.
Turnover through dealers was a modest US$178 million.
Dealers said they saw only banks entering the market to square their commercial positions.
"Nothing really happened. There was almost no speculation at all," said one dealer.
Dealers said the central bank liberalisation should help expand the market's turnover and trigger more volatile trading, but only gradually.
"The expanding fluctuation will only happen when the Taiwan dollar has some direction," another dealer said. "Right now, nobody has interest in trading and the Taiwan dollar has no direction at all."
Dealers said they expected narrow-range trade in the near term, forecasting a tight T$27.49-27.50 range for Saturday.
